Given an integer $n > 1$ and an $n \times n$ grid colored with three colors (black, white, gray). A coloring is symmetric if each cell on diagonal $AC$ is gray and every pair of cells symmetric about $AC$ are both the same non-gray color. Gray cells are labeled $0$, white cells positive integers, black cells negative integers. A labeling is $k$-balanced ($k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$) if: i) symmetric cell pairs have the same label from $[-k,k]$; ii) when a row and column meet at a black cell, the positive integers in that row and column are disjoint; when they meet at a white cell, the negative integers are disjoint.
a) For $n = 5$, find the minimum $k$ admitting a $k$-balanced labeling for the given grid.
b) For $n = 2017$, find the minimum $k$ such that every symmetric coloring admits a $k$-balanced labeling.
